questions.q: The IT Act received its major amendment in —
questions.solution: The **2008 amendment** (effective 2009) added 66C identity theft, 66D cheating, 66F cyber-terrorism and CERT-In's statutory role.

questions.q: A nibble consists of how many bits?
questions.solution: A nibble is half a byte: 4 bits. A byte is 8 bits; a word is CPU-dependent (16/32/64 bits).
questions.shortcut: Nibble = half a byte = 4 bits ('nybble nibbles off half').

questions.q:
Match the Excel shortcut:
A. Ctrl+D  B. Ctrl+R  C. Ctrl+;  D. Alt+Enter
options: A-fill right, B-fill down, C-current time, D-new line in cell
A-fill down, B-fill right, C-current date, D-new line in cell
A-fill down, B-new line in cell, C-current date, D-fill right
A-current date, B-fill right, C-fill down, D-new line in cell
questions.solution: **D down, R right, ; date, Alt+Enter line-break.**

questions.q: The keyboard shortcut for Italics in MS Word is —
questions.solution: **Ctrl+I = Italic**; Ctrl+K inserts a hyperlink, Ctrl+J justifies, Ctrl+P prints.

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (1).
questions.solution: The exchange scheme is the *cause* of the change: because every plastic bag was swapped for a cloth one, visitors stopped bringing plastic at all. The main clause ('visitors slowly gave up…') is the direct result of the scheme, so **Because** fits. *Although* would claim the scheme did not stop them — yet the visitors asked for the cloth bags themselves, which is the scheme working, not failing.
questions.shortcut: Ask: is the main clause the working of the first clause (because) or a surprise against it (although)?
questions.passage: The hill temple at Pachaimalai banned plastic bags five years ago, and the change began at the gate. (1) ______ the staff exchanged a cloth bag for every plastic one handed over at the gate, visitors slowly gave up carrying plastic altogether. (2) ______ the ban, monkeys used to scatter torn plastic along the paths; the slopes are clean now, and pilgrims often photograph them. The ban has even spread beyond the temple; (3) ______, the village panchayat passed a similar rule for its weekly market.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The new taxation policy will have a far-reaching ___ on small traders.
questions.solution: After the article *a* the blank must be a noun, and the meaning is 'result': **effect**. *Affect* is the verb; *affection* is fondness; *effectiveness* needs no 'a far-reaching' frame and changes the meaning.

questions.q: Select the correctly spelt word.
questions.solution: **Hygiene** is pronounced HY-jeen: an 'ee' sound after g, not c, so the pair is **ie**. The word ends in a single n and a final e.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

Sita is / the most intelligent / girl in / a class.
questions.solution: A noun made specific by the superlative phrase and the limiting phrase 'in...' takes **the**: *the most intelligent girl in the class*. 'A class' leaves the noun unidentified and unidiomatic.

questions.q: Which of the following is a **vector** quantity?
questions.solution: **Velocity** is speed in a stated direction, so it is a vector. Speed, mass and energy have only magnitude — scalars.

questions.q:
Match the inscriptions:
1. Ramappa temple — Telangana, 2021
2. Maratha Military Landscapes — 2025
3. Sarnath Buddhist site — 2026
Which are correct?
questions.solution: All three: Ramappa (Telangana, 2021), the Maratha fort landscapes of Maharashtra-Tamil Nadu (2025), and Sarnath (2026) — India's most recent inscriptions.

questions.q: The scientific name of **neem** is —
questions.solution: ***Azadirachta indica***. Mango is *Mangifera indica*, banyan *Ficus benghalensis*, rice *Oryza sativa*.

questions.q: For which of the following payment categories has a higher UPI per-transaction limit of ₹5 lakh (against the usual ₹1 lakh) been provided?
options: Payments to hospitals and educational institutions
questions.solution: **Hospitals, educational institutions, capital markets and insurance** carry ₹5 lakh per-transaction limits; the usual UPI cap is ₹1 lakh.
questions.shortcut: Big bills (health, education, markets, insurance) = ₹5 lakh.

questions.q: If $a+b+c=9$, $ab+bc+ca=11$ and $abc=6$, then the value of $a^3+b^3+c^3$ is:
In a class of 40 students, 30 play hockey, 25 play football and 20 play cricket. What is the maximum number of students who play none of these games?
questions.solution:
The union is at least $\max(30, 25, 20) = 30$.
None $\le 40 - 30 = 10$.

questions.q: Two shooters fire at a target. Their probabilities of hitting it are 1/2 and 1/3, independently. What is the probability that both hit the target?
questions.solution:
Independent events: multiply.
$\dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{1}{6}$.

questions.q: How many integers $x$ with $-5 \le x \le 5$ satisfy $|x - 1| < 3$?
questions.solution:
$-3 < x - 1 < 3$ gives $-2 < x < 4$.
Integers: $-1, 0, 1, 2, 3$ — five of them.

questions.q: In a certain code language, **'sum of money' is written 'ni mo za'**; **'sum earned' is written 'mo ka'**. What is the code for of?
questions.solution: 'sum' is common → sum = mo. 'Of' can be 'ni' or 'za' — two codes remain → **cannot be determined**.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Melon, Melody, Mellow, Member.** Which pair sits on **adjacent** slots?
questions.solution: 4th letters: o (Melon), o (Melody), l (Mellow), b (Member) → Member, Mellow, then Melody (5th d) before Melon (5th n). Order: Member, Mellow, Melody, Melon → the last two are adjacent: **Melon and Melody**.
questions.shortcut: Write the numbered order; adjacency is just slots differing by one.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Angel, Angle, Anger, Amble, Amber.** Which word comes **fourth**?
questions.solution: AM group first (Amber, Amble; B < L), then the ANG group at the 4th letter: Angel (E) and Anger (E) precede Angle (L). Angel vs Anger splits at the 5th: L < R. Order: Amber, Amble, Angel, Anger, Angle → fourth = **Anger**.
questions.shortcut: First-letter split (AM/AN), then compare at the first difference only.

questions.q: Arrange as in a dictionary: **Mystery, Mystic, Myself, Myopia.** Which comes **first**?
questions.solution: MY common. 3rd letters: s (Mystery, Mystic, Myself) vs o (Myopia); o < s → **Myopia** first, whatever happens later. (Full order: Myopia, Myself, Mystery, Mystic.)
questions.shortcut: The earliest 3rd letter ends the contest at once — check the o-word first.
